projects.title: Cave Story Nintendo DS Native Port
projects.status: A public native DS source port based on the CSE2 decompilation. The README documents a devKitPro/libnds make build and Japanese, SD-card, and DSi build options. It lists sound and flashcart caveats and says the two-screen graphics mode is unfinished. This is not a decompilation of a Nintendo DS binary.
projects.summary: Ports the CSE2 Cave Story engine to Nintendo DS homebrew and adds DS-specific code. The README describes the original game-derived code as proprietary and identifies custom modifications as MIT-licensed.
projects.strategy: CSE2 source port to Nintendo DS using devKitPro and libnds
projects.source_available: Public source, Makefile, and build instructions; the README says most original game code remains proprietary, while custom modifications are MIT-licensed.
projects.subtype: Nintendo DS homebrew port; README also documents DSi and Japanese build options

projects.title: Conker's Bad Fur Day Vita Recompilation
projects.status: v1.1.0 was released on 2026-10-14. The maintainer reports in-game saves, sound, music, cutscenes, and 29–30 FPS in the rainy opening on a real Vita. Only the US ROM is supported.
projects.summary: Native Vita port of the N64 game statically recompiled to C with N64Recomp. It uses a Vita sceGxm renderer and runs the game's audio microcode on the Vita CPU. Releases contain no game files; the player supplies a supported US ROM.
projects.strategy: Static recompilation of the N64 game via N64Recomp, paired with a Vita-specific renderer and audio implementation.
projects.source_available: Public release repository and Vita source branch; no game files are included, and the US ROM must be supplied by the player.

projects.title: Donkey Kong 64 Decompilation
projects.status: Public in-progress MIPS decompilation. The maintainer README tracks overall and per-module progress and documents a build from a user-supplied U.S. ROM. GitLab project metadata reports last activity on 2026-10-06; the README's embedded progress graphic was not text-readable during this check, so no percentage is asserted.
projects.summary: A public source decompilation of Donkey Kong 64 for Nintendo 64. The README identifies the U.S. base ROM by SHA-1 and provides extraction and build instructions; it does not distribute the ROM.
projects.strategy: Nintendo 64 MIPS decompilation and ROM reconstruction
projects.source_available: Public GitLab source and tools; the user must supply the U.S. baserom.us.z64 (SHA-1 cf806ff2603640a748fca5026ded28802f1f4a50).

projects.title: Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker Decompilation
projects.status: The repository README identifies the European NTR-AJRP-EUR release and claims 7,140 functions decompiled into 279,930 lines of pseudo-C across ARM9, ARM7, and three overlays. This is maintainer-reported source coverage; the checked README does not document a byte-matching ROM build.
projects.summary: A public Nintendo DS reverse-engineering repository with pseudo-C source, extraction tools, and technical documentation for Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker. The README reports function coverage but does not establish a matching rebuilt ROM.
projects.strategy: ARM9/ARM7/overlay code analysis, pseudo-C decompilation, and asset extraction
projects.source_available: Public GitHub repository containing source, tools, documentation, and extracted game data; no ROM-reconstruction procedure was identified in the checked README.
projects.subtype: European Nintendo DS release NTR-AJRP-EUR; matching build not documented in the checked README

projects.title: Final Fantasy IV / Final Fantasy II SNES Disassembly
projects.game: Final Fantasy IV (Japan) / Final Fantasy II (North America)
projects.platform: Super Nintendo Entertainment System / Super Famicom
projects.status: The public 65816 assembly disassembly documents builds for Japanese Final Fantasy IV 1.0/1.1 and North American Final Fantasy II 1.0/1.1. Users provide the original ROM data, run make rip, then assemble a selected version. The README demonstrates an identical rebuild for U.S. version 1.0; the Japanese Easy Version is unsupported.
projects.summary: A public assembly disassembly and reassembly project for four SNES/Super Famicom releases of Final Fantasy IV. It uses version-specific data extracted from a user-supplied ROM and does not distribute ROMs.
projects.strategy: 65816 assembly disassembly and version-specific ROM reassembly with ca65/ld65
projects.source_available: Public assembly source and tooling; users provide original Japanese and/or U.S. ROMs for data extraction. The README says the repository does not include copyrighted ROM data.
projects.subtype: Japanese Final Fantasy IV 1.0/1.1 and North American Final Fantasy II 1.0/1.1; Japanese Easy Version unsupported

projects.title: Pomme
projects.game: Mac OS 7–9 games written for the Macintosh Toolbox C API
projects.platform: Classic Macintosh Toolbox APIs → modern cross-platform builds through SDL; used by macOS, Windows, and Linux game ports
projects.status: Public source repository. The README describes a deliberately partial Toolbox implementation, says complete source compatibility is out of scope, and lists eight games ported with Pomme. No GitHub release is listed.
projects.summary: A cross-platform partial reimplementation of Macintosh Toolbox C APIs for porting source code from Mac OS 7–9 games. It covers selected classic file/resource, QuickDraw 2D, Sound Manager, QuickTime, and 3D data functions. It is a library for source ports, not a runtime for unmodified classic Mac binaries.
projects.strategy: Partial Macintosh Toolbox API reimplementation for source ports

projects.title: Quesa
projects.platform: Apple QuickDraw 3D APIs → macOS and Windows using OpenGL 3.2
projects.status: The public C++ repository describes Quesa as the reimplementation of Apple's QuickDraw 3D API and reports that rendering was upgraded to OpenGL 3.2. The README identifies the current maintainer and recent camera and FilamentViewer work. No GitHub release is listed.
projects.summary: A BSD-licensed 3D rendering and scene-graph library that reimplements Apple's QuickDraw 3D APIs for macOS and Windows applications. It handles QuickDraw 3D concepts and the 3DMF object format through a modern OpenGL renderer; applications use the library at source/build time rather than loading old Mac binaries.
projects.strategy: QuickDraw 3D API and scene-graph reimplementation using OpenGL

projects.title: Super Mario Bros. C: NES to PS Vita
projects.status: The 0.1 VPK release (2026-05-05) is described by the maintainer as fully playable at 60 FPS with audio disabled for stability. Audio remains experimental and may cause crashes; the user must supply the supported US PRG0 ROM.
projects.summary: Automated C++ translation of the original game's disassembly, built as a Vita VPK. The project retains game-specific NES CPU, PPU, APU, and controller emulation components, so it is a hybrid recompilation with NES hardware emulation rather than a generic NES emulator.
projects.strategy: Automated C++ code generation from the game's NES disassembly, with a game-specific hardware compatibility layer for Vita.
projects.source_available: Public source, code-generation tools, and VPK release; no ROM is included and the player supplies the supported US PRG0 image.

projects.title: Switchyard Wine (Apple Silicon Wine Runtime)
projects.platform: Windows i386/x86-64 software → macOS on Apple Silicon; published Wine runtime reports an x86-64 host build
projects.status: Public downstream Wine runtime with signed and notarized release archives. The latest listed runtime release, 34a0917, reports that Overwatch 2.23.1.1 reached the logged-in main menu with a separately supplied Game Porting Toolkit 4.0 beta 1. The release identifies an x86-64 host runtime and i386/x86-64 PE targets; this is a setup-specific result, not a general compatibility guarantee.
projects.summary: A downstream Wine runtime and reproducible build pipeline for Switchyard on Apple Silicon macOS. It carries targeted macOS compatibility changes, including D3DMetal bridging, MSync, Chromium/CEF rendering, media, and font fixes. The release contains Wine only; Switchyard uses user-supplied Apple Game Porting Toolkit files for the tested GPTK graphics path.
projects.strategy: Wine-based Win32 API compatibility with targeted macOS runtime and D3DMetal fixes
projects.source_available: Public source repository; Wine runtime archives are separately published
projects.subtype: Downstream Wine compatibility runtime for Apple Silicon macOS
